Questions about Birmingham

What is the doh of Birmingham?

In this version, in Eb major, doh is Eb. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Birmingham start on?

It starts on d (E♭ in Eb major). Find doh first, then sing up or down to d.

What words can be sung to Birmingham?

Birmingham is in the metre 10.10.10.10: lines of 10, 10, 10, 10 syllables. Words written in the same metre fit it, such as Breathe Thoughts of Pity O'er a Brother's Fall, Cheer Up, My Soul, There Is a Mercy-seat, Father Divine, This Deadening Power Control; check where the stresses fall before you sing them together.

Is Birmingham in the public domain?

Yes. Rev. F. Cunningham's work dates from 1834; the tune was first published in 1834. Everyone named died before 1955 and it was published before 1929, so the tune is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements of it can still be under copyright.
